points.description: States the basic structure: a two-layer (bipartite) network with a visible layer and a hidden layer of binary neurons.
points.partial_credit: Half if only mentions visible/hidden or binary neurons vaguely.

points.description: States the working principle: neuron states are flipped/set stochastically with a probability determined by the neuron's activation, and/or the learning uses a clamped phase (visible tied to input) and a free-running phase.
points.partial_credit: Half if only says it is probabilistic or has two phases, without detail.

rubric.notes: Full marks for conveying the core idea in any wording: a two-layer visible/hidden network of binary units whose states change probabilistically based on activation. Give part marks for a vague or incomplete but related answer (e.g. only the structure or only the probabilistic behaviour). Clamped/free-running phases are a bonus route to P2 but not required; give no marks for unrelated or wrong descriptions.
